newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr tripped by Howard rate comments.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr tripped by Howard rate comments.

text.p: The Australian dollar dipped suddenly in thin afternoon trading as the market reacted nervously to comments on interest rates from Prime Minister John Howard.

Howard, speaking to a Liberal Party gathering, said; "One of the reasons why interest rates have come down in Australia, and I'd like to see them still lower ... is that we are no longer running such large deficits."
Traders were unsure if he was referring to commercial bank rates, money market rates or official rates -- or all three -- but decided to assume the worst and cut their dollar holdings.
By 2.00 pm (0400 GMT) the local dollar had crumpled to US$0.7423/28 from US$0.7444/49 just before the comments were reported and US$0.7440/45 late here Monday.
Traders suspected Howard's office might clarify his remarks later as only referring to bank rates, but the inference of political pressure would not be lost on offshore investors.

"There was a lot of talk around the last cut that the politicians had leant on the RBA," said one, referring to the Reserve Bank's official easing of May 23. "Comments like this don't help the bank's image of independence, whether he (Howard) meant them that way or not."
Traders said the local currency had been quoted as low as US$0.7417, exceeding the overnight trough of US$0.7420 and a level not seen since January 1996.
There was some chart support at US$0.7390 and US$0.7350 but little in the way of major technical levels until 73 cents, which marked the low for January last year.

The market has been fretting about the risk of a fifth rate cut since the last easing to 5.50 percent brought official rates down to U.S. levels for the first time in over a decade. Money rates have half priced in a move and were easing further this afternoon. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1818
